document.title: Personal Memorandum from Andropov to Brezhnev, early December 1979
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Afghanistan: Lessons from the Last War
document.note: Unusual personal memo that, per Anatoly Dobrynin, was especially influential in changing Brezhnev's position on sending troops into Afghanistan. Source: CWIHP Bulletin 8-9, pp. 159-160.

events.description: Coup against and murder of Taraki; Amin takes power
Andropov memo proposing Soviet military assistance to Karmal and Sarwari to oppose Amin
Coup in Kabul and murder of Taraki, with Amin taking power.
April revolution brought the PDPA to power in Afghanistan.
Amin began mass arrests of 'suspect persons'; 300 people reportedly shot.
Soviet contacts with Babrak Karmal and Asadullah Sarwari, who presented a plan against Amin and requested possible assistance including military.
Andropov memo to Brezhnev proposing a military operation in Afghanistan with a force near the border as backup.

key_claims: Andropov told Brezhnev that after Taraki's murder Amin's repressions had essentially destroyed the party, army and government apparatus.
The KGB reported Amin's alleged contacts with an American agent and promises to tribal leaders of a policy of neutrality.
Karmal and Sarwari, in contact with the Soviets, asked for assistance including military.
Andropov argued two battalions in Kabul were sufficient, with a military group near the border as a precaution.
The operation was framed as defending the April revolution and securing Soviet positions.
